title: Royal Canin Medium Adult vs Josera Daily Menu Adult Duck

key_ingredients.name: Dried poultry protein, wheat, maize meal, wheat flour, maize, hydrolysed animal proteins, animal fat

alternative.product: Josera Daily Menu Adult Duck, 12.5 kg

key_ingredients.name: Wholegrain maize, rice, dried poultry protein, dried duck protein, beet fibre, poultry fat

summary: Both are complete dry foods for adult dogs on zooplus.ie, and the Josera costs about 36% less per kg.
evidence: Both prices were read on zooplus.ie product pages on 2026-11-07, tax included, at the one-time price rather than the Repeat price. Royal Canin Medium Adult 10 kg is EUR 63.49 (EUR 6.35/kg). Josera Daily Menu Adult Duck 12.5 kg is EUR 50.99 (EUR 4.08/kg). Royal Canin's 15 kg pack is EUR 79.99 (EUR 5.33/kg) but was sold out that day, so we compare the 10 kg. Once it's back, the gap is about 23%. Both are sold as complete food.
differences: Royal Canin has more protein and fat: 25% and 14% against 22% and 11% (Royal Canin's figures from zooplus.de). Its recipe is made for medium dogs, and the Josera is for adult dogs of all breeds. The Josera rating is from only 3 reviews. The two rely on different proteins: the Josera has dried duck and poultry protein, and the Royal Canin has poultry protein and hydrolysed animal proteins.
why: The labels show the same everyday job. The sources read don't show whether Royal Canin's extra protein and fat or its sized kibble change results for a healthy dog of this size.

title: Royal Canin Instinctive in Jelly vs Felix As Good As It Looks

brand.product: Royal Canin Instinctive in Jelly, 12 x 85 g

key_ingredients.name: Meat and animal by-products, vegetable protein extracts, minerals, vegetable by-products, oils and fats, yeasts

alternative.product: Felix As Good As It Looks, 44 x 85 g, chicken, beef, tuna and salmon

key_ingredients.name: Chicken pouch: meat and animal by-products (14%, of which chicken 8%), vegetable protein extracts, fish and fish by-products, minerals, sugar

summary: Both are complete wet food for adult cats, sold as chunks in jelly in 85 g pouches, and the Felix costs about 70% less per kg.
evidence: Both prices were read on zooplus.ie product pages on 2026-11-07, tax included, at the one-time price rather than the Repeat price. Royal Canin Instinctive in Jelly 12 x 85 g is EUR 17.49 (EUR 17.15/kg). Felix As Good As It Looks 44 x 85 g, chicken, beef, tuna and salmon, is EUR 19.49 (EUR 5.21/kg). Both pages call the food complete. The Felix rating covers the listing's flavours together.
differences: Royal Canin has more fat, 4.5% against 2.5%, with protein about the same at 11.9% and 11.5%, and slightly less moisture at 80% against 82%. zooplus.de's feeding guides give a 4 kg cat 2.5 Royal Canin pouches a day and up to 4 Felix, so the saving per day is about half, well below the saving per kg. The Felix pack mixes four flavours.
why: The labels show the same everyday job, and even after Felix's bigger portions it comes to about half the cost per day. No taste or feeding test covers this pair.
